newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil inmates free captives, end jail uprising.
newsitem.headline: Brazil inmates free captives, end jail uprising.

text.p: Inmates at a Brazilian jail laid down shivs, knives and other homemade weapons on Tuesday and freed their last 10 hostages, ending a three-day uprising that left two dead, police said.
Civil police Investigator Maria Tereza Soares told Reuters at least five children were among the captives released by prisoners at the overcrowded Ferraz de Vasconcelos jail outside Sao Paulo.
An 8-month-old baby and a 3-year-old child were carried out of the jail by police when the ordeal ended, a Reuters photographer said.
Soares said inmates halted their rebellion at 3:15 p.m. (1815 GMT) on Tuesday after authorities transferred 20 prisoners to other facilities and police had regained control of the jail.
"For the moment, everything's calm," Soares said.

Prisoners rioted during visiting hours on Sunday afternoon, killing two inmates and seizing 15 hostages, including seven children, police said. Five captives were released on Monday as inmates and officials neared an accord.
Inmates were protesting harsh living conditions at the jail, including overcrowding. Soares said the jail, which was built to hold 24 inmates, held 130 late on Tuesday.
Riots are common at Brazil's notoriously overcrowded jails and prisons and the country has been wracked by a rash of uprisings this year, including more than 50 in Sao Paulo state.
